title: RT-qPCR: counting mRNA by cycles
objective: Explain how RT-qPCR turns mRNA amount into a cycle-threshold number.

steps.title: From mRNA to a number
steps.body: **[[RT-qPCR]]** first copies mRNA into cDNA (reverse transcription), then amplifies it, doubling each cycle. A dye reports product in real time. The **[[cycle threshold|cycle threshold (Ct)]]** is the cycle where signal crosses a line — **more starting mRNA → fewer cycles → lower Ct**.

steps.prompt: Sample A has Ct = 20, sample B has Ct = 25 for the same gene. Which started with more mRNA?
steps.explanation: Lower Ct = crossed threshold sooner = more template to begin with. Each cycle ≈ a doubling, so 5 cycles ≈ ~32×.

variants.setup: Gene X: Ct 20 in A, Ct 25 in B.
variants.prompt: Where is there more X mRNA?
variants.reveal: Lower Ct means the template reached threshold sooner — more starting mRNA.

steps.setup: You forget the reverse-transcription step and run qPCR straight on RNA.
options: Little or no signal, since the polymerase needs a DNA template
Normal amplification, since the primers anneal to RNA too
A lower Ct, since RNA is more abundant than the cDNA copy
steps.reveal: The polymerase amplifies DNA, not RNA. No cDNA, no product — which is also why a 'no-RT' control catches genomic DNA contamination.

variants.prompt: Skip reverse transcription and qPCR the RNA directly. Result?
options: Little or no signal, with no DNA template present
Normal curve, since the primers bind the RNA too
A lower Ct, since RNA outnumbers cDNA copies
variants.explanation: qPCR needs a DNA template; RNA alone won't amplify.

steps.title: Each cycle doubles
steps.body: Because amplification is exponential, small Ct differences are big fold-changes: ΔCt of 1 ≈ 2×, ΔCt of 3 ≈ 8×, ΔCt of 10 ≈ ~1000×. That sensitivity is the point — and the reason sloppy pipetting shows up loudly.

sources.citation: Bustin SA et al., 2009, Clin Chem
sources.note: MIQE guidelines: rigorous qPCR, reference genes, reporting.
